take: Brent holding above $100 with the Hormuz crisis now spreading to Saudi export routes via the 10 September attacks on the East-West Pipeline is the dominant story, and with Standard Chartered flagging a higher oil floor and US pump prices at records, the crude and product complex is pricing a genuine supply-risk premium rather than a headline spike. The freight transmission is already violent — tanker rates topping $1 million a day for the first time ever, with the IMO having verified 80 attacks around Hormuz and at least 22 seafarers killed — which simultaneously lifts delivered crude costs and makes tonne-miles a lottery that no charterer can hedge cleanly. On the positioning side, the EIA's forecast of record US crude output at 13.8 million b/d in 2026 and 17.4 Bcf/d of LNG exports in H1 (up 23% year on year) are the only genuine bearish offsets, whilst the record-wide New England gas discount to Henry Hub signals that domestic supply is not the constraint — logistics and risk appetite are. The cross-market link to watch is bunker: with Brent above $100 and HSFO/VLSFO pricing off the same crude complex, shipowners face a double hit from fuel and freight, and the US House's 216-211 vote to overturn California's shore power rule risks stranding over $550 million of port electrification investment just as alternative-fuel lifecycle work (SGMF's methanol assessment) tries to normalise the transition case. For the next 24 hours, watch the Fed decision and any Saudi confirmation on East-West Pipeline throughput restoration, plus whether capesize strength holds given Splash247's warning that Chinese steel demand cracks are forming beneath the hot market.
